memory_candidates.content: A research report's enumerated call-site counts ('three continue branches', 'the directive_stop at line 736-738') are hypotheses to re-grep at plan time, not facts to phase against. Verifying task 109's report against live source found two undercounts: literature-ingest.sh has FOUR no-cleanup continue branches (the 'conversion reported success but no .md file found' branch was missed), and literature-ingest-online.sh has TWO ONLINE_INGEST_PIPELINE_FAILED directive_stop sites (resolvable path and existing-no-pdf attach path), not one. A plan phased against an undercount silently descopes the missed sites -- the implementer edits exactly what the plan enumerates and reports success. Cheap mitigation: before writing phases, run one grep per asserted count against the current file, and attach a Scope Hypothesis line naming the confirming command to every phase that carries a count. Line numbers cited in a research report are especially untrustworthy since they drift; anchor on function names and guard conditions instead.
